The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:76 — The dedupe is case-sensitive, never dedupes within the input array, and never excludes the organizer, so duplicate attendee rows (and the organizer as a guest) can be inserted.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — There is no cap on the guests array and any attendee can call it repeatedly, making it an open relay for sending scheduled-event emails and calendar invites from the platform to arbitrary addresses.

adjudication.rationale: The new TRPC mutation `addGuests` accepts `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max(...)` limit (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts). In the handler, authorization explicitly allows any existing attendee to call it (`const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email);` and only forbids if none of admin/organizer/attendee match). The handler then creates new attendee records and triggers calendar attendee updates and email sending (`eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(...)` and `sendAddGuestsEmails(...)`). Because there is no cap and the mutation can be called repeatedly to add fresh addresses, this enables abuse/spam (sending invites/emails from the platform/organizer to arbitrary addresses).

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:158 — EventManager is built with the caller's credentials instead of the organizer's, so when an attendee or admin adds guests, the organizer's calendar events referenced by booking.references never get updated.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the calendar update is performed via `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` using an `EventManager` constructed from the *caller* (`...user`) and `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` (line ~158). The handler already loads the booking’s organizer user including `credentials` (`include: { user: { include: { credentials: true }}}`), but those organizer credentials are never used. If a non-organizer (e.g., an attendee permitted by `isAttendee`, or a team admin/owner) invokes this mutation, the EventManager will not have the organizer’s calendar credentials, so updating the organizer’s calendar event referenced by `booking.references` is likely to fail or be skipped.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:165 — Attendees are committed to the DB before updateCalendarAttendees runs outside a try block, so a calendar failure returns an error to the client while guests stay saved with no emails or calendar sync.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the mutation first persists new attendees via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` and only afterwards calls `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` without any surrounding `try/catch` or transactional rollback. If `updateCalendarAttendees` throws, the TRPC mutation will error back to the client while the DB changes (new attendees) remain committed; additionally, the email sending is after that call and thus would not run, leaving guests saved without calendar sync/emails.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168 — Emails get the raw `guests` input instead of `uniqueGuests`, so an existing attendee included in the input receives a fresh "scheduled" email instead of the add-guests notice.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, new attendees are computed as `uniqueGuests` (filtered to exclude existing attendees and blacklisted emails), but the email sender is called with the raw `guests` input: `await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests);`. In `sendAddGuestsEmails`, the `newGuests` array controls whether an attendee gets `AttendeeScheduledEmail` vs `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail` via `if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email))`. If the input includes an email that was already an attendee (and thus excluded from `uniqueGuests`), that existing attendee will still match `guests.includes(...)` and receive a fresh "scheduled" email instead of the add-guests notification.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:26 — Booking status and time are never checked, so guests can be added to cancelled, rejected, or past bookings, which sends them confirmed invites.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler fetches the booking by `id` and proceeds to `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` and then sends calendar updates/emails without any guard on booking state or timing (no checks against `booking.startTime`/`booking.endTime`, nor any cancellation/status fields). The email/ICS payloads generated in `attendee-add-guests-email.ts` and `organizer-add-guests-email.ts` hardcode `status: "CONFIRMED"`, so if this mutation is invoked for a past or non-active booking it will still send confirmed invites.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74 — The read-then-createMany flow has no transaction or unique constraint, so concurrent requests can insert the same guest twice.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the code reads existing attendees (prisma.booking.findFirst include attendees) and then later does a separate prisma.booking.update with attendees.createMany based on that earlier snapshot. There is no transaction wrapping the read+write in the diff, so concurrent requests could both decide the same email is “unique” and attempt to insert it. Whether this becomes an actual duplicate-row bug depends on DB-level uniqueness constraints on the attendee records, which are not shown in the diff, so the “no unique constraint” part can’t be verified here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:170 — The email-failure catch drops the error object and still returns success, so notification failures pass silently.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the email send is wrapped in `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` and the handler then returns `{ message: "Guests added" }` regardless. This does drop/log no details from `err` and makes email notification failures non-obvious while still treating the mutation as successful. However, the primary action (adding guests + updating calendar attendees) has already completed, so this is more an observability/UX concern than a clear correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — Server schema lacks the client's uniqueness refine (and non-empty/lowercase normalization), so direct tRPC callers can submit duplicate emails that get inserted as duplicate attendees via createMany.

adjudication.rationale: The server-side input schema `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` only enforces `z.array(z.string().email())` and does not enforce uniqueness. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` filters out emails that already exist on `booking.attendees` and blacklisted ones, but it does not de-duplicate duplicates within the `guests` payload itself. Therefore a direct tRPC caller can submit `["a@b.com", "a@b.com"]` (or case variants) and both entries will pass the filter and be inserted via `attendees.createMany` as duplicate attendee rows (unless there is an unseen DB unique constraint, which is not shown in the diff).

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168 — sendAddGuestsEmails receives raw input `guests` instead of filtered `uniqueGuests`, so already-existing attendees included in input are sent a fresh "scheduled" email instead of the add-guests notice.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the mutation filters input into `uniqueGuests` (excluding existing attendees/blacklisted) and only adds those to the booking. However it later calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the raw input array. In email-manager.ts `sendAddGuestsEmails(calEvent, newGuests)` checks `if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email))` to decide to send `AttendeeScheduledEmail` (intended for newly added guests) vs `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail` (intended for existing attendees). Passing raw `guests` means any existing attendee email included in the input will incorrectly receive a fresh scheduled email instead of the add-guests notice.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:77 — Blacklist check lowercases the env list but compares the un-normalized guest email (and attendee dedupe is case-sensitive), so mixed-case input bypasses both.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the blacklist is normalized to lowercase (`BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS.split(...).map(email => email.toLowerCase())`), but the comparison uses the raw `guest` string (`!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`), so a mixed-case input like `Test@Example.com` can bypass the blacklist. Similarly, attendee de-duplication is case-sensitive (`guest === attendee.email`), so mixed-case variants can be added as “new” even if the email already exists with different casing. The diff shows no normalization of `guests` before these checks.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:43 — Error message template string is always truthy, so the `unable_to_add_guests` fallback is dead and raw "undefined: ..." can be shown.

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog.tsx` `onError`, `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;` always produces a non-empty string (e.g., `"undefined: ..."`), so `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")` will never use the fallback. If `err.data?.code` is missing, the toast can show a raw `undefined:` prefix as the finding states.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:46 — isTeamAdmin && isTeamOwner requires both roles, so team admins (non-owners) are wrongly denied; should be OR
matched_golden_ids: The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same permission logic bug: using `isTeamAdmin && isTeamOwner` incorrectly requires both roles and should be `||` so either admin or owner is allowed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74 — Blacklist is lowercased but guest emails are not, so mixed-case blacklisted emails bypass the filter (attendee duplicate check is also case-sensitive)

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, blacklistedGuestEmails are normalized to lowercase (split(...).map(email => email.toLowerCase())), but the incoming `guest` strings are compared without normalization: `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. This allows a mixed-case email (e.g., `Test@ex.com`) to bypass a lowercase blacklist entry (`test@ex.com`). Similarly, the duplicate check `guest === attendee.email` is case-sensitive, so the same email with different casing can be added again. Both issues are directly verifiable from the diff and can lead to incorrect behavior/bypass of intended filtering.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74 — Server schema/filter does not dedupe guests within the input, so duplicate emails create duplicate attendee rows

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:158 — EventManager uses the acting user's credentials rather than the organizer's, so calendar attendee updates fail/miss when an attendee or team admin adds guests

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:165 — updateCalendarAttendees errors are uncaught after attendees are already persisted, returning an error to the client while DB is changed and emails are skipped

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:43 — Toast message is always a non-empty template string so the unable_to_add_guests fallback is dead and shows "undefined: ..." when code is missing

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:165 — Calendar update runs after the attendee DB write with no try/catch or rollback, so a calendar/API failure returns an error while guests stay persisted (and a retry fails as "not unique" and never syncs the calendar or sends emails).

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the DB is updated first via prisma.booking.update(...attendees.createMany...) and only afterward calls await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking) with no try/catch and no compensating rollback. If the calendar update throws, the mutation errors out while the new attendees remain persisted. A subsequent retry will compute uniqueGuests by filtering out existing booking.attendees and can hit the `uniqueGuests.length === 0` BAD_REQUEST path, preventing calendar sync/emails from ever succeeding for those guests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:92 — The duplicate check and createMany are not atomic or in a transaction, so concurrent or double-submitted requests can insert duplicate attendee rows.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the handler reads the current attendees (booking.attendees) and computes uniqueGuests by filtering against that snapshot, then performs prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}}) without a transaction/locking or any Prisma-level dedupe (e.g., skipDuplicates) and without showing any DB unique constraint in this diff. That means concurrent/double-submitted requests can both pass the pre-check and then both create the same attendee rows, resulting in duplicate attendees for the booking (or a late unique-constraint error if such a constraint exists).

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:159 — EventManager is built from the caller's credentials rather than the booking organizer's, so when an attendee or team admin adds guests the calendar update fails or targets the wrong account.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the handler explicitly allows non-organizers to add guests (permission check allows isAttendee or team admin/owner), but then builds the EventManager from the caller (`const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user); const eventManager = new EventManager({ ...user, credentials })`). The booking organizer is separately loaded (`organizer = await prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ id: booking.userId })`) and `booking.user` (including credentials) is fetched but never used for EventManager. This means when an attendee/admin triggers the mutation, `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` will run under the caller’s calendar credentials instead of the booking organizer’s, plausibly failing to update the organizer’s calendar event or updating the wrong account.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168 — sendAddGuestsEmails gets the raw `guests` list instead of `uniqueGuests`, so existing attendees included in the input get a duplicate "scheduled" email/ICS.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler filters input emails into `uniqueGuests` (excluding existing attendees and blacklisted emails) and only persists `uniqueGuests`, but then calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the raw `guests` input. In `email-manager.ts`, `sendAddGuestsEmails` treats any attendee whose email is in `newGuests` as a “new guest” (`if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email))`), so if the caller included an existing attendee email in the input, that existing attendee will still match and receive another “scheduled” email/ICS even though they weren’t newly added. Passing `uniqueGuests` (or otherwise deriving newly-added emails) is required to avoid this duplicate email behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:77 — The blacklist is lowercased but guest emails are not, and the attendee dedupe is case-sensitive, so mixed-case input gets past both checks.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:158 — EventManager runs with the caller's credentials instead of the booking organizer's, so an attendee or admin caller drives calendar/video updates against the organizer's booking references using their own connected accounts.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the mutation allows non-organizer callers (attendee or team admin/owner) to proceed past the permission check, but then builds the EventManager using the caller’s session user and credentials: `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] })`. It then calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`, meaning calendar updates for the booking are attempted with the caller’s connected accounts rather than the booking organizer’s (whose credentials were already included on `booking.user` but are not used). adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:47 — isTeamAdmin && isTeamOwner requires both roles instead of either, so the team-admin authorization path is wrong (it only works for owners).

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, which requires the user to be both a team admin and a team owner to pass that branch. This contradicts the variable name and the intended authorization check implied by the finding (admin OR owner). As written, a team admin who is not also an owner will be denied unless they are also the booking organizer or an attendee, which is a real behavioral/authorization defect introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:46 — Authorization logic (admin AND owner, organizer, attendee, forbidden) is untested and the `&&` bug that locks out team admins would be caught by a single permission test.

adjudication.rationale:
In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed with `&&`:
```ts
const isTeamAdminOrOwner =
  (await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) &&
  (await isTeamOwner(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0));
```
This requires the user to be both a team admin and a team owner to pass the team-role check, which will incorrectly deny access to admins who are not owners (and owners who are not admins). That directly affects the subsequent permission gate:
```ts
if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw FORBIDDEN;
```
So the diff introduces/exposes a real authorization bug; the “untested” part is not verifiable from the diff, but the `&&` logic defect is.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx:418 — The MultiEmail add/remove/edit index handling has no tests (and the index keys risk stale input values after a removal).

adjudication.rationale: The finding’s line reference is incorrect (new `packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx` is ~96 lines, not 418), but the underlying concern is diff-grounded: `MultiEmail` renders a dynamic list with `key={index}` (`value.map((field, index) => <li key={index}>...)`) and supports removal via `splice(index, 1)`. Using index keys in an editable/removable list is a known footgun and can cause item-to-input mismatches if the child (`EmailField`) has any internal state. The diff also introduces this nontrivial add/remove/edit behavior without any accompanying tests visible here.
